# Wikimedia Outreachy sample

Small, sanitized excerpts captured on **2026-11-13**, not current application
availability or eligibility advice. Text is by the MediaWiki contributors and
is redistributed under [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).
Attribution and contributor histories:

- [Outreach programs](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Outreach_programs)
  ([history](https://www.mediawiki.org/w/index.php?title=Outreach_programs&action=history))
- [Outreachy](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Outreachy)
  ([history](https://www.mediawiki.org/w/index.php?title=Outreachy&action=history))

Changes: retain the directory's two canonical Outreachy anchors, the programme's
real nested heading, lead paragraph and resource links. Remove images, scripts,
styles, language controls, edit controls, unnecessary attributes, historical
editions and unrelated footer content. No executable source content is retained.
`capture.json` distinguishes the complete decoded response hashes from the
reduced fixture hashes; only allowlisted response headers are retained.

Access basis (checked 2026-11-13):

- [Robot policy](https://wikitech.wikimedia.org/wiki/Robot_policy) explicitly
  permits low-rate reads of canonical `/wiki/Article_name` URLs without queries.
- [User-Agent policy](https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Wikimedia_Foundation_User-Agent_Policy)
  requires identification and contact information. The live validation used
  `DiscMonValidationBot/0.1 (https://github.com/arulx06/DiscMon; bounded programme validation)`.
- [robots.txt](https://www.mediawiki.org/robots.txt) allows both article paths;
  `/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/...` is disallowed and was never followed.
- [Terms](https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use) allow reuse
  subject to attribution/share-alike and prohibit abusive automated access.

Only one programme candidate was evaluated. The public directory is Wikimedia's
own outreach listing; its Outreachy page states Wikimedia participation and
funding. Canonical article URLs and long-lived participation make a useful
stable overview, but the article is not an authoritative live application
window or a complete eligibility policy. No linked external site was fetched.

The parser currently labels the full article and this excerpt `mentorship`
from the mentor resource link. This is a recorded heuristic result, not proof
of a particular open round. Wikimedia is explicit source configuration, not an
inferred legal employer. The application URL falls back to the official article;
no actual application endpoint, remote status, salary, deadline, or India
eligibility is claimed. HTTP Last-Modified is not a programme publication date.
